heads: Exports near $90 billion in October; goods shipments hit a record
Iran says it hit a US radar in Bahrain; tanker blast in Hormuz
New Zealand crush India by 244 runs in fourth ODI

paras.t: Namaskar, and welcome to Pringital News. Credible like print, fast like digital. This is your four-minute bulletin for Friday, the thirteenth of November, twenty twenty-six, from New Delhi.

First, the headlines. India’s exports have climbed to nearly ninety billion dollars in October. Iran says it has struck a U.S. radar in Bahrain. And New Zealand have handed India a heavy defeat in the fourth one-day international.

India’s total exports of goods and services rose nearly thirty per cent to eighty-nine point nine nine billion dollars in October. Merchandise exports alone touched a record forty-nine point four seven billion dollars. But imports grew faster, and the goods trade deficit reached a one-year high of thirty-nine point eight eight billion dollars. A strong services surplus narrowed the overall gap to about twenty billion dollars. On Dalal Street, the Sensex fell three hundred and nineteen points and the Nifty closed at twenty-five thousand, one hundred and forty-four, as traders braced for a possible rate hike by the Reserve Bank in December.

Iran’s Revolutionary Guards say they targeted a U.S. early-warning radar in Bahrain, home to the U.S. Navy’s Fifth Fleet, in retaliation for a strike in southern Iran. The Guards also say an L.P.G. tanker exploded after hitting a mine in the Strait of Hormuz. President Donald Trump says Gulf allies have asked him to hold off major strikes, but he is not sure he agrees. For India, which ships much of its crude and cooking gas through the strait, oil prices remain above ninety dollars a barrel.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi is in Bengaluru today, launching projects worth over fifteen thousand six hundred crore rupees. They include a new Vande Bharat Express linking Bengaluru, Mangaluru and Madgaon in Goa. Earlier, at a farmers’ conference, he said the government absorbed forty-three rupees of a possible fifty-rupee rise in diesel prices during the West Asia conflict. The Prime Minister will also attend the ASEAN–India summit in the Philippines next week.

Travellers will soon fill shorter visa forms, with up to seventy per cent fewer fields and a new Visitor Visa. The Comptroller and Auditor General has begun its first combined audit of thirty-nine state power distribution companies. And ISRO has successfully ground-tested a modified third stage of the P.S.L.V. rocket.

European delegates will join the next round of Russia–Ukraine peace talks, President Volodymyr Zelensky and U.S. envoy Jared Kushner have said. In Haiti, police have retaken the national football stadium from gangs after two years. And millions of people marched across Spain over the housing crisis.

At Mount Maunganui, Will Young scored one hundred and twenty-five and Matt Henry took six wickets as New Zealand beat India by two hundred and forty-four runs. India still lead the series two–one, with one match to play. India’s under-nineteen team are in the Asia Cup final, and shooter Vivaan Kapoor has won trap silver and a quota place for the Los Angeles Olympics.

Ramayana has crossed seven hundred and fifty crore rupees worldwide in six days. Kangana Ranaut will star in a Telugu horror film, Scary Picture. And Karan Johar says he wants to direct three more films before he turns sixty.

If your cat meows at you, it may be asking for help. Researchers in Brazil found that pet cats meowed far more at a hidden treat when a person was watching: eighty-six times, against just twenty when they were alone. Cat owners, it seems, already knew.

That was your Pringital News bulletin, the day’s important news in four minutes. For the full story, tap the link on your Pringital page. Read it on your phone, share it on WhatsApp, and help save the trees cut for newsprint. Thank you for listening. Namaskar.
